rules.title: Ban on certain algorithmic rent-setting software
rules.requirement: Santa Ana landlords may not use rent-setting software that relies on nonpublic market data, such as real-time rents, lease activity or occupancy, to set rents. If a landlord used such software, you can sue by showing it was used, without proving collusion.
rules.key_value: up to $1,000 per violation, plus damages, injunctive relief and attorney's fees

coverage.summary: All residential rental housing in Santa Ana. Tools that rely on publicly available data, historical trends, or are used for affordable housing compliance are not restricted.

rules.exemptions: Does not restrict tools that rely on publicly available data or historical trends, or tools used for affordable housing compliance.
rules.penalty: Tenant civil action for damages, injunctive relief, up to $1,000 per violation, and attorney's fees.
rules.citation: Santa Ana algorithmic rent-setting ordinance (adopted March 3, 2026; ordinance number not stated)
rules.quoted_span: The Santa Ana City Council has adopted a new ordinance to strengthen renter protections by limiting the use of certain rent-setting software for residential properties.
rules.interaction: The newsletter describes the ordinance as complementing broader state-level protections.

notes: Source is an official city newsletter summarizing the ordinance; it gives the approval date (March 3, 2026) but no effective date or ordinance/code number. Status is set to in_force on the assumption that it took effect well before 2026-10-01; confirm against the ordinance text. Other references to the Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance contain no specific rules, so none were extracted.
